report.denominator: This reports the decisions UIR REQUIRES, not the whole of good design. WCAG has criteria UIR does not model and never claims to, so a design system that has stated everything on this checklist is one that has decided everything this language asks — not one that is accessible, and not one that is good. And STATING is the weakest word in that sentence: every line here says whether something was stated, never whether what was stated means anything.

report.populationNote: Almost every demand a package raises is raised by a record it holds, so every count over that ledger moves in BOTH directions when the population changes and nothing about the design does: deleting records deletes their demands, and adding records that raise cheap, fully answerable demands adds holdings without limit. Splitting it by SUBJECT CLASS did not close that and this contract no longer says it did; nor did moving the ratio onto the reference profile's own demands, which is a denominator a package cannot raise and was still read as wholly met by a package whose every intent-bearing prose member is the string 'x'. So no ratio is computed at any grain, and what the reference profile states is read as a CHECKLIST: its demands are fixed before the package is opened, a record can neither add one nor delete one, one record is credited at one of them at most, and every line says WHERE it was stated. It is deliberately small, it names the contract sentence under every row, and where the language states no count — of Pieces above all — it states none, so eleven of the twenty-one subject classes are asked nothing and say so. What no checklist can reach is what an answer SAYS: a demand answered with the string 'x' is stated here, the compiler's own rules already refuse junk at every typed position, and what is left is prose no mechanical test can judge. Two design systems are comparable on what the language states of both, and on nothing else; `docs/GAPS.md` carries the rest rather than the measurer inventing a bound.
report.publicationRule: NO RATIO IS COMPUTED OVER AN AUTHORED PACKAGE — no headline, no per-class share, none over the reference profile's demands, none over the accessibility half, in no presenter and nowhere in the payload. A ratio over an authored package is free, because a record costs nothing to write and no measurer can read what it says: the blended headline read a well-decided package with every component deleted as most of a design system; split by subject class, 2,000 `Register` Entities answering their own two demanded members read that class as wholly decided; and moved onto the reference profile's fixed demands, a package the compiler ACCEPTS read 48 of its 48 units as decided with every intent-bearing prose member replaced by the string 'x'. What is published instead is a CHECKLIST — for each thing the reference profile expects, stated or not stated, and where, by record id and address — beside counts and the lists under them. Junk passes a checklist too. The difference is that a checklist never CLAIMED to be a quality measure, which is exactly what a percentage claims and cannot support. WHAT THIS IS NOT is a claim that a reader cannot compose one. Both sides of a ledger have to be published, and two counts in one unit divide; so every count here travels with the statement of which denominator it stands over, and there are exactly two — one this package's own author moves, and one the language fixes before the package is opened, which is the width of one Fact of a kind and the reference profile's own minima. The one ratio this toolchain does sell is the conformance DEGREE, which is grounded on both sides: both come from reading real files, and nobody can invent a class name that is not in the source.
report.recordKeepingNote: A Fact about where a statement came from, or about where a decision is absent, is record-keeping and not a decision about the design. It is counted apart and enters neither the debt nor the holdings, because a headline made of the reader's own bookkeeping says nothing about the design system it claims to measure.
report.rejectedNote: An answer this reading REFUSED answers nothing — presence was never the question. The refusal attaches to the DEMAND the diagnostic addresses and to no other, so a finding about one member never costs the credit for another and a finding about a record that is NOT there costs nothing at all; a position the package left empty is undecided rather than refused, because nothing was stated there to refuse. What a reading refused weighs exactly what it always weighed, stays on the undecided side because a developer must still invent it and must now repair the record as well, and is named as its own class so that 'nobody wrote it' and 'somebody wrote something invalid' are never one number. A demand is joined to what this reading said about it by the record's ADDRESS, which every record has, and never by an `id`, which a package can omit. WHICH demands one finding refuses is declared by the code that raised it wherever an address cannot say — a finding anchored on a record and naming nothing inside it is either about that record's own standing, and then no position of it answers anything, or about a demand the record merely raises, and then it costs nothing at all; those two wear one address and are never told apart by its shape. No count in this report can be raised by authoring a record the compiler rejects.

report.selfRaisedNote: A COUNT IS NOT COMPARABLE BETWEEN TWO PACKAGES, and it is published with the population that raised it for exactly that reason. Almost every demanded position a package holds is raised by a record it holds, so deleting records deletes the debt: on `@exams/ui` `delete-pieces` of all 386 Pieces takes 'what a developer must invent' from 58,071 to 47, BELOW the 48 an EMPTY package owes. Split, it is 42 comparable units plus 5 raised by the package's own records against an empty package's 48 plus 0, and only the first half is a number two design systems can be read against. Adding records moves it the other way without limit. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO IS MAKE A RATIO UNREACHABLE. Both sides of one ledger are published — the debt because it is the debt, and the holdings because a report that credits nothing a package decided is as useless as a percentage that can be faked — and two counts in one unit ADD. This contract publishes no quotient, no percentage and no total of the two at any grain, and it says here rather than leaving a reader to find out that adding its published counts recovers one: 393 answered positions and 58,071 undecided ones on `@exams/ui`. It does not compute that, does not print it and does not endorse it; it cannot prevent a consumer computing it, because two commensurable counts are arithmetic and no rule about output reaches arithmetic. NOR IS THE DENOMINATOR WITHHELD, and a sentence here once said it was: an accessibility line carries `stated` and the population that raises it on one line, a class ledger carries both of its sides, and every one of those has to be printed, so the operands are on the page by necessity. What it CAN do is say AT every count which denominator that count stands over — one this package's own author moves by writing records, deleting them, or writing a larger minimum in a profile layer he owns, or one the language fixes before any package is opened — and that is what it does.
report.uncheckedNote: What could not be checked is reported and never counted as a pass. A reading that silently treats unread things as fine is worse than no reading.
report.waiverNote: The accessibility half is not a ratio and no longer has one. It is one LINE per demanded member position — how many records state it, how many decline it, how many leave it, how many answer it with something this reading refused, how many of the statements say there is nothing to state, and how many BYTE-DISTINCT things were said at it — with the population that raises those positions on the same line and the records that state it named under it. A `waiver` or an `external` Gap THIS READING ACCEPTED is a decision and counts as one in the whole, where the question is how much a developer must invent; it raises `declined` and can never raise `stated`, because the accessibility half is a claim about a property and deciding not to state that property is not the property. An accepted waiver names the Obligation it waives, a Source for the decision and a rationale; an accepted external Gap names a rationale and, required exactly of an external Gap, WHERE the realization lives instead — a placement naming nowhere is a refusal to state, and is refused as one. A Gap this reading REFUSED names nothing: it raises neither, it stays where it always was on the undecided side, and it is reported as `refused`. Waiving accessibility everywhere, and having it accepted, reads every position declined and none stated. THE DISTINCT COUNT IS NOT A DEFENCE AGAINST A PLACEHOLDER: 386 claims differing only in a rotating integer are 386 distinct claims here, and one varying token defeats it. It sees byte-sameness and nothing else.

diagnostics.message: a `contrast` design.constraint is typed and never evaluated. The shape phase requires a colour foreground, a colour background and a positive minimum, and no phase resolves the two DesignValues to literals and compares their computed ratio against that minimum, so ground.md GRD-09's "applicable computed contrast obligation" is stated by the package and decided by nobody. It is named here rather than implemented because ground.md says a threshold is computed and says with WHICH computation nowhere — WCAG 2 relative luminance and APCA disagree about which pairs pass — and choosing one here would be coding a rule no document states. docs/GAPS.md carries the line; T5.1 reports the gate it makes unchecked, and an unchecked gate is never counted as a pass

the parent-role axis still ranges over its whole DECLARED domain instead of the Roles the claimed containment graph actually produces, and two things follow that a reader must not mistake for safety. Demands are raised at parent Roles no occurrence carries, which OVER-demands; and a package.prohibition over that axis is doing real work only because of this over-approximation — once the narrowing lands such a prohibition is either vacuous or a claim the package's own contains Relations refute, so it must be refused then, and the refusal is deliberately not made now because it would remove the only way to say so today

the total resolution algorithm runs over the reachable evaluation POINTS and all ten Piece compatibility checks run there; two of them enforce only the members the contracts give a predicate for. accessibility decides the contribution mode, activation, focus, name and the state exposure a supported RequiredState owes, but not whether "reading order, Asset purpose and reflow obligations fit the Node need": piece.accessibility largestTextScale, localizedRange and readingOrder are load-bearing Facts no contract gives a predicate for, and the exposure demand stops at a merged Piece because v0.1 names no merge owner. measure decides the declared bounds ordering, the growth mode and the inline fit in the preview frame, but not what wrap, truncation, distribution, the largest claimed text scale or the localized content range require there. All of them are contract sentences rather than missing code; docs/GAPS.md carries them

two slot obligations are decided by no phase. A slot whose fillKinds is exactly ["asset"] has neither its minimum nor its maximum checked: the child-use phase skips every slot without a piece fill and the evaluation-point phase skips every slot no Node fill reaches, so an asset-only slot falls between them. Separately, a piece.measure whose three declared bounds do not share one unit skips BOTH the ordering check and the fixed-growth equality check, because the comparison gives up instead of reporting that it cannot compare
